newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SriLankan forces widen search for missing aircraft.
newsitem.headline: SriLankan forces widen search for missing aircraft.

text.p: Sri Lankan air force planes and navy patrols have widened the search for a helicopter gunship missing off the island's northeastern coast, a Defence Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
"So far, nothing has been found," he said. "The search is still on."
It was not clear if the Mi-24 helicopter, missing since Wednesday, was shot down by Tamil Tiger rebels, who control large areas of the east and northeast, he said.

Two pilots, a Sri Lankan and a Russian, and a Russian technician were on board the Russian-built helicopter, believed to have gone down off the coast of northeastern Mullaitivu, 280 km (175 miles) from the capital Colombo, he said.

But a Tamil Tiger rebel-controlled newspaper published in the north quoted fishermen off Mullaithivu as seeing a fireball in the sky about the time the helicopter went missing, said residents in the frontline army-held town of Vavuniya.
The rebels' Voice of Tigers radio station, monitored by Reuters, only quoted news reports from Colombo saying the aircraft was missing.
The Defence Ministry said two Mi-24s took off from the Palaly base in the northern Jaffna peninsula at around 10.45 a.m. (0445 GMT) heading east on Wednesday.
The trail helicopter was reported missing around 12.45 p.m. (0645 GMT). The other helicopter landed safely.

Mi-24s are part of the air force's attack fleet used in the war against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of this predominantly Sinhalese island.
Sri Lanka's tiny air force has already lost six aircraft this year in operations against the rebels.
A Pucara ground attack aircraft exploded over the northeastern Polonnaruwa district on Saturday after the pilot had ejected safely.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the civil war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
